methodology: Review the source resource, adapter locator construction, fixture metadata, and raw artifact dimensions for every HEAD source.
Call geometry verified only when the adapter preserves a provider-backed coordinate transform and the fixture or contract contains control-point evidence.

An official image-overlay transform with explicit bounds applied to the exact timeline paths is provider-backed geometry; retain the source bounds and derive pixel-center controls from the actual raw dimensions.
A declared bounding box, projection name, or tile URL is locator evidence; it is not evidence that the provider pixel grid is scientifically native.
Do not infer a curvilinear grid from a rendered image. Require retained two-dimensional longitude/latitude arrays or equivalent provider geometry metadata.
curvilinear_evidence: The 24 HEAD fixtures contain image/tile artifacts or blocked manifests; none contains two-dimensional longitude/latitude coordinate arrays.
The adapter implementations expose regular geographic, tile-locator, or unverified image geometry only.
tests/contract/test_grids.py covers the existing CurvilinearGrid model, but no source currently supplies a real curvilinear payload.

conclusion: RainViewer and the numeric tw:grid product now have source-backed regular-grid transform evidence among the 24 HEAD sources. tw:observation PNG and tw-http remain blocked independently. No real two-dimensional curvilinear source was found, so the existing CurvilinearGrid contract is retained without adding a source-specific curvilinear adapter. The remaining unverified products and historical CPTEC/SIPAM lines require verified native pixel geometry and physical value semantics; rows without canonical raw data also require an attributable payload before scientific acceptance.
